title: Correlating Optical and Structural Properties of Core/Shell GaN Nanowires ​for Optoelectronic Applications Using Advanced Electron Microscopy​
content: Achieving higher efficiency is a major focus in the light emitting diode (LED) industry, aiming to maximize light output while minimizing energy consumption. Nanowire LEDs present a promising alternative to planar LEDs, offering advantages such as high surface-to-volume ratio, dislocation-free structures, non-polar facet exposure, and tunable axial and radial growth. Despite these benefits, nanowire-based devices are still in their early stages, facing challenges related to doping, strain, impurities, and point defects—factors that critically influence their structural, optical, and electronic properties. In this study, we employ advanced electron microscopy techniques to investigate how these properties evolve in GaN nanowires as they transition from axial core growth to radial shell growth.
